intro: Pour opposer deux idées, « but » ne suffit pas toujours. « Although », « however » et « despite » permettent d'exprimer la concession (« bien que », « cependant », « malgré ») de façon plus nuancée, à l'oral comme à l'écrit. Mais chacun a sa propre construction : proposition, nom ou phrase séparée.
objectifs: Utiliser although / though / even though + sujet + verbe.
Utiliser despite / in spite of + nom, + -ing ou + the fact that.
Placer however et nevertheless correctement, avec la bonne ponctuation.
Transformer une phrase d'une structure à l'autre sans changer le sens.

texte: Ces mots expriment tous un contraste : la deuxième idée est surprenante ou inattendue par rapport à la première. La différence est grammaticale : ce qui vient après le mot.
Une erreur très fréquente vient du français : « malgré » est suivi d'un nom, « bien que » d'un verbe ; c'est pareil en anglais (despite + nom, although + verbe), mais « despite of » n'existe pas.

lignes: It was raining, but we went out.
Although it was raining, we went out.
Even though it was raining, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
It was raining. However, we went out.
It was raining. Nevertheless, we went out.

texte: Ces conjonctions introduisent une proposition complète (sujet + verbe). Elles peuvent se placer en tête de phrase (suivie d'une virgule) ou au milieu.

« Though » est plus courant à l'oral. « Even though » renforce le contraste (« alors même que ») et s'utilise pour un fait réel. À l'oral, « though » peut aussi se placer en fin de phrase avec le sens de « pourtant » : « It was expensive. I bought it, though. »
Attention : on ne met pas « but » dans la même phrase qu'although (« Although it was late, but… » est incorrect).
exemples: Although she was tired, she finished the report.
Bien qu'elle soit fatiguée, elle a fini le rapport.
I enjoyed the trip to Kinshasa, though it was very hot.
J'ai aimé le voyage à Kinshasa, même s'il faisait très chaud.
Even though he earns a lot, he never has any money.
Alors même qu'il gagne beaucoup, il n'a jamais d'argent.
The hotel was nice. The food wasn't great, though.
L'hôtel était bien. La nourriture n'était pas terrible, cela dit.

texte: « Despite » et « in spite of » ont exactement le même sens. Ils sont suivis d'un nom, d'un pronom ou d'un verbe en -ing, jamais directement d'une proposition.
Pour ajouter une proposition complète, on utilise « despite the fact that » / « in spite of the fact that » + sujet + verbe. Ne jamais écrire « despite of ».

lignes: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
In spite of his age, he still plays football.
Despite feeling ill, she went to work.
Despite the fact that it was late, the shop was open.

exemples: We enjoyed the evening despite the rain.
Nous avons passé une bonne soirée malgré la pluie.
In spite of working hard, he didn't get a promotion.
Bien qu'il ait travaillé dur, il n'a pas eu de promotion.

sections.titre: However et nevertheless : liens entre deux phrases
texte: « However » est un adverbe de liaison : il relie deux phrases séparées, pas deux propositions dans une même phrase. On le met généralement en début de deuxième phrase, suivi d'une virgule ; il peut aussi se placer au milieu, entre virgules.

Dans une seule phrase, on peut utiliser un point-virgule : « It was raining; however, we went out. ». Mais « It was raining, however we went out » (une simple virgule) est considéré comme incorrect à l'écrit.
« Nevertheless » et « nonetheless » ont le même sens, plus formel : ils conviennent bien aux rapports et aux e-mails professionnels.
exemples: The project was difficult. However, the team finished it on time.
Le projet était difficile. Cependant, l'équipe l'a terminé à temps.
The new phone is expensive. It is, however, very fast.
Le nouveau téléphone est cher. Il est cependant très rapide (au milieu, entre virgules).
Sales fell in March; nevertheless, the company made a profit.
Les ventes ont baissé en mars ; néanmoins, l'entreprise a fait un bénéfice.

texte: Il est très utile (et fréquent dans les examens) de savoir passer d'une construction à l'autre. Avec despite, il faut trouver un nom ou une forme en -ing qui correspond au verbe : « it rained » → « the rain » ; « he was ill » → « his illness » / « being ill ».

lignes: Although he was ill, he came.
He was ill. However, he came.
Although she has a lot of experience, she didn't get the job.
Despite her experience, she didn't get the job.
She has a lot of experience. However, she didn't get the job.

formule: although / even though + sujet + verbe · despite / in spite of + nom / -ing · Phrase 1. However, phrase 2.
prononciation: « although » /ɔːlˈðəʊ/ : accent sur la 2e syllabe, th sonore /ð/, le gh est muet.
« though » /ðəʊ/ rime avec « go » ; ne pas confondre avec « through » /θruː/ ni « thought » /θɔːt/.
« however » /haʊˈevə/ : accent sur la 2e syllabe ; à l'oral on marque une petite pause après : However, | we…
À la fin d'une phrase, « though » est prononcé avec une intonation légèrement descendante-montante : It was good, though.
erreurs: Despite of the rain, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out. / In spite of the rain, we went out.
despite sans of ; in spite of avec of.
Although it was late, but we continued.
Although it was late, we continued.
Pas de but avec although.
Despite it was raining, we played.
Although it was raining, we played. / Despite the rain, we played.
despite + nom / -ing, pas une proposition.
It was expensive, however I bought it.
It was expensive. However, I bought it. / It was expensive, but I bought it.
however relie deux phrases (point ou point-virgule).
Although the traffic, we arrived on time.
Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
Devant un nom seul : despite.
In spite of be tired, he worked.
In spite of being tired, he worked.
Après in spite of : -ing.
Even she was ill, she came.
Even though she was ill, she came.
even seul n'est pas une conjonction : even though.

dialogue.contexte: Deux amis, Didier et Sandrine, parlent à Liège du nouveau travail de Didier.
lignes: I like it, although the hours are long.
Ça me plaît, même si les horaires sont longs.
Do you have to commute every day?
Tu dois faire le trajet tous les jours ?
Yes. Despite the distance, it only takes forty minutes by train.
Oui. Malgré la distance, ça ne prend que quarante minutes en train.
Most are great. My manager is quite strict. However, she's always fair.
La plupart sont super. Ma responsable est assez stricte. Cependant, elle est toujours juste.
And the salary? You didn't seem sure about it.
Et le salaire ? Tu n'avais pas l'air convaincu.
It's lower than at my old job. I'm much happier, though.
Il est plus bas que dans mon ancien poste. Je suis beaucoup plus heureux, cela dit.
That's what matters. Even though money is important, it's not everything.
C'est ce qui compte. Même si l'argent est important, ce n'est pas tout.

mots: Although it was cold, we swam.
Despite the noise, I slept well.
It's cheap. However, it's not very good.
It was risky. Nevertheless, they did it.
There's a big contrast between the two cities.
I commute to Brussels every day.
My manager is strict but fair.
Despite her experience, she didn't get the job.

items: ___ the bad weather, the match went ahead.
Despite
___ he studied hard, he failed the exam.
Although
The hotel was cheap. ___, it was very clean.
However
She went to work ___ having a headache.
despite
___ I don't like football, I watched the final.
Although
The plan is good. It is, ___, very expensive.
however

exercices.consigne: Complète avec la forme correcte après despite / in spite of (nom ou -ing).
items: Despite ___ (be) very young, she runs her own company.
being
In spite of ___ (the / delay), we caught our connection.
the delay
Despite ___ (not / speak) French, he found a job in Quebec.
not speaking
Despite ___ fact that it was Sunday, the shop was open.
the

exercices.consigne: Réécris la phrase avec le mot entre parenthèses, sans changer le sens.
items: Although it was raining, they had a picnic. (despite)
Despite the rain, they had a picnic.
Despite being tired, he went out. (although)
Although he was tired, he went out.
The car is old, but it works well. (however)
The car is old. However, it works well.
She didn't get the job although she had good qualifications. (in spite of)
She didn't get the job in spite of her good qualifications / in spite of having good qualifications.

exercices.consigne: Chaque phrase contient une erreur. Réécris-la correctement.
items: Despite of the cost, we bought the house.
Despite the cost, we bought the house.
Although he was rich, but he wasn't happy.
Although he was rich, he wasn't happy.
Despite she was ill, she came to the meeting.
Although she was ill, she came to the meeting. / Despite being ill, she came to the meeting.
Even I was late, they waited for me.
Even though I was late, they waited for me.
Malgré la grève, j'ai pu aller au travail.
Despite the strike, I was able to get to work.
Bien qu'il soit timide, il a fait un excellent discours.
Although he is shy, he made / gave an excellent speech.
Le restaurant était cher. Cependant, le repas était délicieux.
The restaurant was expensive. However, the meal was delicious.

exercices.consigne: Écris un court paragraphe (5 phrases) sur les avantages et les inconvénients de ta ville ou de ton travail, avec although, even though, despite et however.
items: Exemple de réponse

I love living in Douala, although the traffic is terrible. Despite the heat, there's always a nice breeze in the evening near the river. Rent is quite high. However, food is still affordable at the local markets. Even though I sometimes miss the calm of my village, I wouldn't move.

a_retenir: although / though / even though + sujet + verbe (Although it rained, …).
despite / in spite of + nom ou -ing (Despite the rain / Despite being tired) ; jamais « despite of ».
however / nevertheless : début de la 2e phrase + virgule, ou après un point-virgule.
Pas de but avec although ; « though » en fin de phrase = cela dit, pourtant (oral).
